TRUMP SAYS OIL PRICES WILL BE A LOT LOWER WHEN THIS IS OVER

First CAS Manipulation found.

SEBI has passed an ex-parte interim order against an FPI and a local stockbroker, for what it calls prima facie manipulation of CAS on 13 August and wrongful gains of ₹3.67 crore.

What really happened?

It was Sensex weekly expiry. Inside the auction window the index moved 362 points in two seconds, then 405 points in 28 seconds.

1. Copthall Mauritius was 86.6% of the entire gross buy value in that auction. Every order across all 30 Sensex stocks at exactly 3% above reference price, the maximum the band allows. Then it cancelled ₹98 crore of them once the move had happened. 

It held long calls and short puts on that expiry. Spent ₹57 lakh in the cash market, made ₹2.96 crore in derivatives.

2. Mansi Share and Stock Broking did the reverse. 

₹145 crore of sell orders below reference price, holding the index down while it exited its long puts, then cancelled 99% of them in three seconds. 

That cancellation alone moved the Sensex 233 points.

JUBILANT INGREVIA: From Pyridine to PCBs

A chemicals company with 45+ years of legacy in pyridine and acetic anhydride just paid ₹189.2 crore for 40% of an electronics design firm. Sounds like random diversification. It isn't.

Jubilant Ingrevia already sells into the semiconductor value chain, just one layer down. Its CDMO arm makes ultra-high-purity chemicals for chip and display manufacturing: E-Pyridine, E-Choline, photoresist precursors, display intermediates. The fab customer relationships already exist.

What Jubilant structurally cannot build in-house is what Zettaone brings. Co-founded about two decades ago, it does R&D, design, prototyping, manufacturing, assembly and box build for aerospace, defence, semiconductor, automotive, medical and industrial customers. The pitch to those shared customers becomes: we don't just supply your chemicals, we can design and build your electronics too.

Zettaone's turnover: ₹51.1cr in FY24, ₹79.1cr in FY25, ₹98.1cr in FY26. Growth decelerating from +55% to +24%.

₹189.2cr for 40% implies roughly ₹473cr for the whole company, about 4.8x sales.

40% makes Zettaone an associate, not a subsidiary. It won't consolidate. Jubilant gets an equity-accounted share of profit and no control over the business it's backing.

A genuinely interesting angle on India's electronics localisation push, entered through a side door nobody was watching.

HEG: NCLT APPROVES DEMERGER; TWO INDEPENDENT LISTED COMPANIES TO BE CREATED 🚀

⚖️ NCLT Indore Bench has approved HEG’s Composite Scheme of Arrangement, clearing a key hurdle for the restructuring.

🔄 HEG will be split into two independently listed companies, separating its mature graphite electrode business from its fast-growing advanced materials and clean-energy businesses.

📊 Share entitlement: HEG shareholders will receive 1 equity share of HEG Graphite Ltd for every 1 share held in HEG Ltd — 1:1 ratio.

🔋 The new growth platform will focus on advanced battery materials, battery energy storage solutions, renewable power and other advanced materials.

🏭 HEG Graphite will house the core graphite electrode business, including one of the world's largest single-site graphite electrode plants.

📌 Scheme becomes effective after receipt and filing of the certified NCLT order with the Registrar of Companies, subject to remaining regulatory requirements.

🟢 Impact: Positive — demerger could unlock value through sharper business focus, independent capital allocation and separate valuation of the graphite and high-growth clean-energy businesses.

SEBI ACTION ON SENSEX CAS EXPIRY MANIPULATION — 2 ENTITIES BARRED

⚠️ SEBI alleges Copthall Mauritius Investment Ltd and Mansi Share & Stock Broking manipulated the SENSEX closing price during the August 13 Closing Auction Session (CAS).

📈 Copthall allegedly pushed SENSEX higher through aggressive buy orders, including orders placed 3% above reference prices across constituents.

📉 Mansi allegedly pushed SENSEX lower, placing aggressive sell orders for 12.65 lakh shares across 8 SENSEX stocks, before subsequently cancelling the entire block.

🎯 SEBI linked the cash-market activity to their expiry-day SENSEX options positions, alleging the trades were intended to influence the SENSEX IEP and generate F&O gains.

💰 SEBI estimates wrongful gains of ₹2.96 Cr for Copthall and ₹71.65 lakh for Mansi — combined ₹3.68 Cr.

🏦 SEBI ordered ₹3.68 Cr to be impounded and kept in fixed deposits with a lien in favour of SEBI.

⛔ Both entities barred from accessing the securities market and participating in the Closing Auction Session until further orders.

🔴 Impact: Negative for market integrity concerns around CAS — SEBI's swift action signals tighter surveillance of expiry-day closing-price manipulation.

Mitsu Chem Plast Limited Q1 FY27 Concall Highlights

Mitsu Chem Plast Limited continues to expand its presence across industrial packaging, healthcare furniture components and value-added plastic products, serving diverse sectors including pharmaceuticals, chemicals, agrochemicals, FMCG, food and healthcare. With four manufacturing facilities and an installed capacity of 32,450+ MTPA, the Company is focused on capacity expansion, product rationalization, margin improvement and new growth opportunities, with a long-term target of ₹1,000 Cr revenue by FY28.

Financial Performance Snapshot Q1 FY27:
* Total Income of ₹ 9,532.78 Lakhs, YoY growth of 11.62%
* EBITDA of ₹ 1,549.48 Lakhs, YoY growth of 209.50%
* EBITDA Margin of 16.29%, YoY growth of 1,041 Bps
* Net Profit of ₹ 873.83 Lakhs, YoY growth of 566.23%
* Net Profit Margin of 9.18%, YoY growth of 765 Bps
* EPS of ₹ 6.44, YoY growth of 563.92%

Capacity Expansion & Manufacturing:
* Incremental capacity will cater to containers, furniture parts and other product categories.
* FY26 capacity utilisation stood at ~64%, with 64–70% considered a healthy operating range.
* Machinery procurement and commercialization typically require 6–9 months, supporting the Company's focus on advance capacity planning.

IBC Entry & New Growth Opportunity:
* Entering the Intermediate Bulk Container (IBC) segment as a new industrial packaging opportunity.
* Commercial production is targeted to commence in Q3 FY27.
* IBC project will require dedicated machinery and new segment is expected to broaden the Company's packaging portfolio and create an additional growth avenue.
* Investment details for the IBC project will be announced separately.

Product Mix & Customer Expansion:
* Healthy demand continues across containers, furniture parts and other value-added products.
* Product portfolio is being rationalised to prioritise higher-margin and better-throughput products.
* Added 30+ new customers in Q1 FY27, following 150+ additions in FY26.
* Focus remains on improving customer quality, throughput and profitability rather than pursuing volumes at the expense of margins.
* Packaging contributes ~80% of revenue, with furniture and other products accounting for the balance ~20%.
* Management expects both major segments to grow while maintaining a broadly similar 80:20 mix.

Margin Improvement & Raw Material:
* Q1 FY27 margin expansion was driven by operating efficiencies, product-mix improvement, innovation, value addition and value engineering.
* Raw material prices have risen amid geopolitical developments and higher crude prices, with the Company largely sourcing domestically.
* Higher raw material costs are generally passed through to customers, with pricing adjustments typically taking ~1 month.
* Operational bottlenecks continue to be addressed to drive further efficiency gains.
* While Q1 EBITDA Margin stood at a strong 16.29%, management considers a sustainable range of ~10–13% with double-digit margins achievable.

Healthcare Furniture & Export Opportunity:
* Furnastra healthcare furniture and components remain a key growth opportunity.
* Furniture parts and other value-added products contribute ~19.8% of revenue.
* Management expects the contribution from furniture and other products to increase as these businesses scale.
* Exports currently contribute ~2% of revenue, offering significant headroom for international growth.
* Company has entered international markets, with global customer relationships currently being scaled up.

Growth Outlook:
* Management expects growth momentum to continue sequentially, with increasing emphasis on profitability and bottom-line growth.
* Long-term revenue target of ₹1,000 Cr by FY28 remains intact.
* Container and furniture-part businesses are being scaled to support the long-term growth target.
* Capacity expansion, IBC entry and product rationalisation are expected to provide additional growth levers.

MM Forgings boss said on their latest earnings call that big data center companies are now placing orders with Indian forging firms 

Data centers need diesel generators as backup power, and every generator needs forged steel crankshafts. India wants to grow data center capacity from 1.8 GW today to 12 GW by 2030, means thousands of new generators will be needed. 

Forging companies that can make heavy crankshafts, like MM Forgings with its new 16,500 ton press, are getting fresh business outside trucks or cars

Indian forging companies made 80% of their money from trucks and cars for years. Now tech giants like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft are building massive data centers in India, and each facility needs dozens of diesel generators for power backup. 

These generators use forged crankshafts, same type forging firms make for heavy trucks. MM Forgings just put up world largest hot forging press and can now produce crankshafts up to 300 kg. Genset makers like Cummins are lining up as buyers. This is fresh demand from outside auto.

If you order backup generators for data centers today, you wait 42 weeks for delivery. Order books at major genset makers are full through 2028. 

India added 258 MW of new data center capacity in H1 2026, up 59% from last year. Each new campus needs 40 to 60 diesel generators on site. Cummins India grew revenue 35% from data center backup orders. 

When generator demand is this strong, forging companies that supply finished crankshafts become important vendors. MM Forgings posted Q1 FY27 sales of 427 crore, up 16%.

The bare board is where India's import substitution story lives

India assembles electronics at scale. But it barely makes the PCB, the board every device sits on. Only 1 in 10 PCBs used in India are made in India. The rest come from China. This gap is the real import substitution opportunity.

The market is worth about Rs 400bn today. It should reach Rs 790bn by 2030, growing at 12% a year. Multilayer boards make up 60% of it, HDI another 25%, flex and the rest fill the last 15%. The value and the moat sit in multilayer and HDI. Anyone serious about this space has to compete there, not at the bottom.

First support comes in to boost local manufacturing is from favourable policy. Customs duty on bare PCBs rose from 10% to 15%. China and Hong Kong now face a 30% anti dumping duty for five years. Behind this sits the Rs 760bn Semicon India programme, funding fabs, OSAT, and design at half the project cost. The government wants local value addition in electronics to nearly double, from 18 to 20% today toward 38 to 40%. A components scheme is also being framed, with PCBs high on the list.

But the base is small. All twelve tracked domestic makers together earned only Rs 34bn in FY24, against a Rs 400bn market. Margins vary sharply too. Micropack runs a 27% EBITDA margin, Circuit Systems 23%, Ascent Circuits 20%. Genus Electrotech and AT&S India barely clear 1 to 2% PAT. Avary and Meena Circuit post outright losses. The spread shows how much scale and product mix decide everything.

Also new capacities are coming fast. Kaynes Semicon is building 25,000 sqm a month in Mysuru, a Rs 14bn bet due in 2026. Ascent Circuits is spending Rs 6.5bn at Hosur, live in 2025. Bonfiglioli, BPL, T Works with Qualcomm, and Schneider Electric are all adding lines too.

And just before calling this a gold rush, look at the global leaders. Samsung Electro Mechanics, Unimicron, Zhen Ding, and TTM Technologies mostly posted mid single digit PAT margins over the last decade, with modest growth and rising debt. AT&S even posted a group loss last year. Bare PCB manufacturing is capital heavy and cyclical. Real pricing power only shows up in HDI and IC substrates. This business rewards patience, tough customer qualification, and staying power through the cycle

India is also building the backend chip ecosystem in parallel. Tata is spending Rs 270bn on assembly and test in Assam. CG Semi and Micron are building OSAT in Sanand. Tata with Powerchip is putting Rs 910bn into a fab in Dholera. 

The setup is clear. A Rs 400bn market doubling by 2030. A 90% import gap. Tariff protection. A subsidy cheque. Demand and policy both point the same way. What is not proven yet is execution: can these lines run at world class yield and cost

One key thing to track here is not just the capacity announcements but how this capacity gets utilised with top teir OEMs
